rationale: Four interpretable density-mode prototypes in the five standardized purchasing-behavior features. Support histograms reveal an online-share gap at 0.50-0.60, a large-basket trough near USD100, and a spend trough near USD2250 among low-online small-basket customers. Define disjoint seed regions once: online_share>0.55 -> digital-first; otherwise avg_basket>100 -> occasional premium; otherwise annual_spend>2250 -> frequent loyal; remainder -> budget regulars. Take each region mean once, without reassignment or iterative fitting. Output order is budget regulars, frequent loyal, digital-first, occasional premium. Raw purchasing-feature means respectively are approximately (1357,5.20,21.07,10.57,0.156), (4077,11.41,34.26,3.67,0.104), (2726,2.58,67.88,14.59,0.859), (5516,1.42,232.09,39.93,0.243). Age has near-zero correlation with all behavior and similar means in the four regions, so its weights are zero; missing indicators are also zero. Linear output row k is 2*c_k and bias is -sum(c_k^2), an exact nearest-prototype circuit with no hidden layers. Weights are derived only from explicit threshold-region means and geometry.
